title: Tiny House Hymn Sheet
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
Source row: QID 21869, Criminal Procedure / Fourth Amendment, tested rule: arrest warrant for a suspect does not by itself authorize entry into a third party’s home without a search warrant or valid exception. The source row gives official key B and states the arrest warrant did not authorize warrantless third-party-home entry absent consent or exigency.

Final Christian variation — “Tiny-House Hymn-Sheet Night”

At Lydia’s tiny house, a private psalm-singing rehearsal has turned into a hymn-sheet stapling contest. Police, holding an arrest warrant for Timothy, get a tip that Timothy is helping there. They have no search warrant for Lydia’s home, no consent, and no emergency. They enter the tiny house and arrest Timothy in the prayer nook.

Call: Was the entry lawful?

choices.A: Yes, because the tip gave officers reasonable suspicion that Timothy was inside.
choices.B: Yes, because an arrest warrant travels with the suspect into any private home.
choices.C: No, but only because Timothy was seized in the prayer nook rather than at the front door.
choices.D: No, because officers needed a search warrant for Lydia’s home or a valid exception.

rightExplanation: D is correct. The entry was into Lydia’s home, not Timothy’s. Gold Key: an arrest warrant authorizes seizure of the named person; it does not itself authorize officers to enter and search a third party’s home for that person. The officers needed a search warrant for Lydia’s home or a valid exception such as consent or exigency. Silver Key: resolve the door before the room. The question asks about crossing Lydia’s threshold, so the prayer-nook detail comes too late to supply entry authority.

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: “Reasonable suspicion” is a lower-threshold authority claim. Gold Key cuts it: third-party home entry requires a search warrant or valid exception.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: “Any private home” is the overbroad portability claim. Gold Key cuts it: an arrest warrant for Timothy does not become a search warrant for Lydia’s home.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: This answers the wrong point in time. The call asks whether officers could enter Lydia’s home; “prayer nook rather than front door” is an interior-location issue after entry.

c3.label: Residual
c3.text: D is true and responsive. No CLASH or CALL needed.

studentScript: Door first. This is Lydia’s home, not Timothy’s. No search warrant, no consent, no emergency. Cut the any-home answer, cut reasonable suspicion, cut the prayer-nook answer. Pick D.

A.signal: The answer uses a suspicion standard to justify crossing a home threshold.
A.lawyer: Reasonable suspicion that the suspect is inside does not substitute for a search warrant or exception for a third party's home.

B.signal: The phrase 'any private home' is the overclaim; the Gold Key tells the student why the scope is too broad.
B.lawyer: An arrest warrant for Timothy does not authorize entry into Lydia's home absent a search warrant or valid exception.

C.signal: The choice answers where Timothy was seized after entry, not whether officers could cross Lydia's threshold.
C.lawyer: The legal defect is the entry into the third party's home, not the prayer-nook location.

D.signal: This is the only choice that answers the threshold-entry call with the missing search warrant or exception.

goldKeys.statement: An arrest warrant lets police seize the named suspect; it does not by itself authorize entry into someone else’s home. For a third party’s home, look for a search warrant for that home, consent, or exigency.
goldKeys.trigger: arrest warrant + suspect located in a third party's home
goldKeys.authority: Steagald v. United States, 451 U.S. 204 (1981); Payton v. New York, 445 U.S. 573 (1980)

silverKeys.statement: When the call asks whether entry into a home was lawful, decide the door before the room. A bedroom, prayer nook, or living room fact cannot supply authority to cross the threshold.
silverKeys.trigger: answer turns on where the suspect was found after entry

remediation.title: Person warrant vs place warrant
remediation.signal: Arrest warrant for suspect + suspect inside someone else's home.
remediation.studentMove: Ask whose home is being entered.
remediation.tinyRule: Own home may be Payton; third-party home needs Steagald search warrant or exception.
